Right: the same triangles joined by C-D and B-D instead; every route between the two sides now passes through D (shown in the accent color), so is_biconnected() returns False." width="100%"} A graph is biconnected if it is connected, has at least two nodes, and stays connected after removing any single node; equivalently, it has no articulation points and forms a single biconnected component. Biconnected networks have no single point of failure: every pair of nodes is joined by two paths that share no intermediate node. A single edge between two nodes counts as biconnected (removing either node leaves one node, which is trivially connected). Graphs with fewer than two nodes are not. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is biconnected, otherwise `False`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle survives the loss of any one node; a path does not: ::: {#cd089785 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) cycle.is_biconnected(), path.is_biconnected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
